qt: to the Commission Ioan-Rareş Bogdan (PPE) Subject:
New CO2 standards risk forcing Romanian hauliers out of the single market

While I welcome the European Commission’s efforts to modernise the transport sector and promote green solutions, the recent revision of the CO2 emission standards for heavy-duty vehicles harbours a series of pitfalls and major structural imbalances that could have catastrophic economic repercussions for Romanian freight and transport fleets. Forcing through a transition to prohibitively expensive electric or hydrogen-powered trucks could, for example, wipe out thousands of independent Romanian SMEs and therefore benefit large Western logistics corporations. Other issues include the near-total absence of highpower recharging and hydrogen refuelling stations along Central and Eastern European transport corridors and the fact that these environmental standards could, in reality, turn out to be trade barriers that will force Eastern European hauliers out of the single market. In the light of the above, I ask the Commission: 1.
Has it carried out an impact assessment to specifically determine the likelihood that ramping up CO2 standards could cause Eastern European road transport SMEs to go under?
How does it justify imposing uniform decarbonisation targets when Romania’s major transit routes are practically bereft of fast-charging stations for trucks?

What specific financial mechanisms will it make use of to fund fleet renewal in peripheral Member States and ensure that these new CO2 standards do not become a means of surreptitiously enforcing protectionist policies?
